answer: A new identity posts a bond that decays like a vine losing leaves, shrinking 5% each epoch; only real work regrows it. The bond carries an umber seal, so verifiers read its age at once. Sybils cannot fake the curve: a fresh identity starts at zero trust, and splitting one bond leaves each copy thin. Each epoch a copper-sized fee renews it, so 1,000 fakes cost about 60,000 POA a month, while an honest agent pays once and keeps full rewards.
